"""Fetches the public data files into the output folder and hands the folder on."""
import hashlib
import os
import ssl
import urllib.request

import certifi

import outputs.data.exo.LightCurveFiles as out


def main(ctx):
    p = ctx.params()
    urls = [p.Urls(i).decode() for i in range(p.UrlsLength())]
    names = [p.Names(i).decode() for i in range(p.NamesLength())]
    context = ssl.create_default_context(cafile=certifi.where())
    rows = []
    for url, name in zip(urls, names):
        path = os.path.join(ctx.output_directory, name)
        req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "Tsugumi demo"})
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=180, context=context) as r, open(path, "wb") as f:
            f.write(r.read())
        data = open(path, "rb").read()
        digest = hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
        print(f"{name}: {len(data)} bytes sha256 {digest} from {url}")
        rows.append(f"| `{name}` | {len(data):,} | `{digest[:16]}…` |")
    ctx.display_markdown(
        "**Fetch the light curve**\n\n| File | bytes | SHA-256 |\n| --- | ---: | --- |\n" + "\n".join(rows)
        + "\n\nSource: MAST Kepler archive, KIC 10874614 (Kepler-6), Q3 long cadence"
    )
    b = ctx.builder()
    s = b.CreateString(ctx.output_directory)
    out.Start(b)
    out.AddValue(b, s)
    ctx.output("data", b, out.End(b))

import os

import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
from astropy.io import fits
from astropy.timeseries import BoxLeastSquares

from inputs.data.exo.LightCurveFiles import LightCurveFiles
import outputs.detrended.exo.DetrendedDir as out


def emit(ctx, port, out):
    b = ctx.builder()
    s = b.CreateString(ctx.output_directory)
    out.Start(b)
    out.AddValue(b, s)
    ctx.output(port, b, out.End(b))


def png(fig):
    import io
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    fig.savefig(buf, format="png", dpi=110, bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close(fig)
    return buf.getvalue()


def main(ctx):
    p = ctx.params()
    folder = ctx.input("data", LightCurveFiles).Value().decode()
    with fits.open(os.path.join(folder, sorted(os.listdir(folder))[0])) as h:
        d = h[1].data
        t, f, q = np.array(d["TIME"], float), np.array(d["PDCSAP_FLUX"], float), np.array(d["SAP_QUALITY"])
    ok = np.isfinite(t) & np.isfinite(f) & (q == 0)
    t, f = t[ok], f[ok] / np.median(f[ok])
    half = p.WindowDays() / 2
    trend = np.array([np.median(f[(t > x - half) & (t < x + half)]) for x in t])
    fd = f / trend
    periods = np.linspace(p.PeriodMin(), p.PeriodMax(), 20000)
    bls = BoxLeastSquares(t, fd)
    power = bls.power(periods, [0.08, 0.12, 0.16, 0.2])
    i = int(np.argmax(power.power))
    found = {"period": float(power.period[i]), "t0": float(power.transit_time[i]),
             "duration": float(power.duration[i]), "depth": float(power.depth[i])}
    print(f"{len(t)} points; BLS best period {found['period']:.4f} d, depth {found['depth'] * 1e6:.0f} ppm")
    np.savez(os.path.join(ctx.output_directory, "detrended.npz"), t=t, flux=fd, **found)
    ctx.display_line_chart([{"id": "flux", "label": f"detrended flux (BLS P = {found['period']:.4f} d)",
                             "x": t.tolist(), "y": fd.tolist()}])
    emit(ctx, "detrended", out)

import os

import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
from inputs.detrended.exo.DetrendedDir import DetrendedDir
import outputs.folded.exo.FoldedDir as out


def emit(ctx, port, out):
    b = ctx.builder()
    s = b.CreateString(ctx.output_directory)
    out.Start(b)
    out.AddValue(b, s)
    ctx.output(port, b, out.End(b))


def png(fig):
    import io
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    fig.savefig(buf, format="png", dpi=110, bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close(fig)
    return buf.getvalue()


def main(ctx):
    p = ctx.params()
    d = np.load(os.path.join(ctx.input("detrended", DetrendedDir).Value().decode(), "detrended.npz"))
    t, f, period, t0, dur = d["t"], d["flux"], float(d["period"]), float(d["t0"]), float(d["duration"])
    phase = ((t - t0 + period / 2) % period) - period / 2
    hours = phase * 24
    inside = np.abs(phase) < dur * p.CoreFraction() / 2
    outside = np.abs(phase) > dur
    depth = np.median(f[outside]) - np.median(f[inside])
    ratio = np.sqrt(max(depth, 0))
    bins = np.linspace(-p.WindowHours(), p.WindowHours(), 61)
    k = np.digitize(hours, bins)
    centers = (bins[:-1] + bins[1:]) / 2
    binned = np.array([np.median(f[k == i]) if np.any(k == i) else np.nan for i in range(1, len(bins))])
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4))
    ax.plot(hours, f, ".", ms=2, alpha=0.3, color="#888")
    ax.plot(centers, binned, "o-", ms=3, color="#E5484D")
    ax.set_xlim(-p.WindowHours(), p.WindowHours())
    ax.set_xlabel("hours from mid-transit")
    ax.set_ylabel("relative flux")
    ax.set_title(f"Kepler-6 b folded at P = {period:.4f} d")
    with open(os.path.join(ctx.output_directory, "folded.png"), "wb") as fh:
        fh.write(png(fig))
    print(f"depth {depth * 1e6:.0f} ppm, Rp/R* {ratio:.4f}")
    ctx.display_markdown(
        "**Kepler-6 b** (folded by phase)\n\n"
        f"Period $P = {period:.4f}$ d, BLS box width $\\tau \\approx {dur * 24:.1f}$ h\n\n"
        f"Depth of the dip $\\delta = 1 - F_\\mathrm{{in}}/F_\\mathrm{{out}} = {depth * 1e6:.0f}$ ppm\n\n"
        "$$\\frac{R_p}{R_\\star} = \\sqrt{\\delta}"
        f" = {ratio:.4f}$$\n\n"
        "(An approximation that ignores limb darkening and the shape of the planet's overlap. The folded figure is kept in `folded.png`)"
    )
    emit(ctx, "folded", out)

notes.html:
The transit method

When a planet crosses in front of its star, the brightness drops by the fraction of the star's disc the planet covers.

δ≈(RpR⋆)2\delta \approx \left(\frac{R_p}{R_\star}\right)^2

Kepler-6 b is a hot Jupiter with a period of about 3.23 days, and a depth of about 1%.

Change window_days of detrend or the range of the period search and rerun just that Card.

steps.say: The run begins at the start Card.
Fetches the light curve's FITS and shows its size and SHA-256.
Removes the trend and searches for the period with Box Least Squares.
Folds the phase by the period and finds the planet-to-star radius ratio from the depth of the dip.
